precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 10:3
precepts.why:
Cain said, “Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: God was not dealing with him anymore. “and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.” A fugitive is somebody always on the run, someone who never pays for his crimes. A vagabond is in everybody's land and everybody's home.

But Cain did not escape forever. Wisdom shows he was put to death: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment caught up with him.

So what did it mean, I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond? It speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet. They have been on the run from justice, living in everybody's land.

That goes with Job 20, read in the same class: “His bones are full of the sin of his youth.” The fugitive has never paid, but as Cain perished in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother, judgment will come on his children. As Job said, “he shall vomit them up again”: everything taken will be restored.

precepts.label: Luke 17:32
precepts.why:
The angels pulled Lot into the house and smote the men at the door with blindness, and even blinded they wearied themselves trying to find the door. Then the angels took Lot out and gave them one order as the cities burned: don't look back. “And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.” “But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.”

Why would she look back? The city was being destroyed; she had just seen what happened in front of her house. She should have been glad to escape. Somebody was not vexed with the filthy conversation of that city; there was something in it she missed. That is why Luke also says, if you put your hand on the plow and look back, you are not worthy.

Christ said it in three words: “Remember Lot’s wife.” That is a warning for all of us: don't look back. You are in this truth now. Stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to be friends with everybody and please people, stop dropping by the house on their birthday. Focus on this truth and stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed just as Lot's wife was destroyed.

Judgment is coming to Esau, as Sodom's came. “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” We have to come out of her mentally, come back to the law, statutes and commandments, stop playing around in the truth, and keep the faith of Christ, without looking back.

thread.label: Genesis 25:21-28

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:7-10
precepts.why:
When the twins were born, Jacob came out and “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind it, and 2 Esdras 6 explains it.

Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” In other words, when shall this world end, and when shall the new world come in? The answer goes straight to Rebekah's womb: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That is what the hand on the heel means. Esau's world is the one that ends, and Jacob's is the one that follows. It matches what the Lord told Rebekah: “Two nations are in thy womb”, “the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” The word Genesis means beginning, and this is the beginning of those two nations.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: all the other nations sit between those two. They are like extras in the movie. Moab is an extra; Ishmael is an extra. The story is Jacob and Esau. Christians do not know what that means at all.

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
Rebekah bore twins, but they were not identical, because the Lord said “two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels.” They looked different. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau means wasted away: his melanin was wasted away. Look at them in a heat wave in France: when they are in the sun they get red. Down south they are called rednecks, but it is not just their necks. Don't call them white; they are Esau, and these are his children.

The scripture never mentions Jacob's color, because Jacob looked just like his mother and father. In fact, Jacob looked like everybody from the time of Adam. Genesis 2:7 shows what that was: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” The dust of the ground is different shades of brown, and the deeper you dig, the darker it gets. That is what Adam looked like, and Eve, and everyone who came from them.

The only one who differed was Esau, and that is why the scribes had to write down his color: he was starkly different. In the old world, Cain's line was cursed with a lack of melanin. The flood came and killed them all off, and God brought them all back through Noah's three sons.

So when you move up the generations to Isaac and Rebekah, the two lines return in one womb. Esau is the return of Cain's lineage, and Jacob is the return of Seth. That is why the two boys were two manner of people from birth: Esau the cunning hunter, a man of the field who liked the rush of the hunt, and Jacob a plain man, dwelling in tents, herding the sheep and the goats.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 8:16-20
precepts.why:
Esau cried, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father.” Jacob had already received the major blessing. Rebekah sent him in, dressed in goats' hair so he would feel hairy like his brother, because she remembered what God told her at the birth: the elder shall serve the younger. When Jacob feared a curse, she said let it fall on her. The white man's the devil, and when you ask the Christians about those two boys, they say Jacob was the evil son and Esau the good one, and black people in church echo those same sentiments. No: Jacob was the good one. Esau was the profane one, the fornicator, the one who despised his birthright, and Rebekah was being obedient to God.

Isaac answered Esau: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” Dew falls everywhere, and wherever it falls, Esau would live; he would have the best places on the planet. How would he get them? “And by thy sword shalt thou live”: by war. God through Isaac blessed Esau with the art of war, the same blessing Cain's line had when Tubal-cain made all kinds of weapons.

Then: “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” When did that first happen? 2 Kings 8 answers. “Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign”, and “he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.” Yet the Lord would not destroy Judah for David's sake. “In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” That is the first time Esau broke the yoke from off his neck, just as Genesis 27:40 prophesied.

After that, Edom turned on his brother outright. When the Babylonians destroyed the first temple in 586 BCE, Edom helped them instead of helping Judah: rejoicing, looting the city, blocking the survivors who fled. Obadiah, “concerning Edom”, says, “even thou wast as one of them”, and “Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape.” 1 Esdras names who set the fire: “the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:43-44
precepts.why:
Exodus 1:11 says “they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” Deuteronomy 28 names that as a curse: “The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low. He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.”

The strangers are the people that were amongst us. They get above us very high, and we come down very low. To be above us means they rule and tell us what to do, and another name for that is taskmaster.

That curse was on us in ancient Egypt: the Egyptians were over us, and we were on the bottom of society. It is the same way the so-called white man and the nations are above us today, and we are the bottom of society. The taskmasters today are the governors, the politicians, the police officers, the FBI agents, people set to keep us in check and keep us in order, with laws like Jim Crow and the black codes to keep us low. On the cotton field there was always a white overseer to make sure we did the work, or you got your ass whooped. Today your taskmaster is your boss.

What was done to us in ancient Egypt is what was done to us in America. That is why this place is spiritually called Egypt.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:30
precepts.why:
“And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.” We built cities in ancient Egypt, and it is the same thing here in America. Deuteronomy 28:30 lists it among the curses: “Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her: thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.”

In ancient Egypt we built cities and houses, and we did not build them for ourselves; we built them for the Egyptians. We were a commodity, and they did not look at us as human. America did the same.

What house did we build here in America and could not dwell in it? The White House. Construction began in 1792 in Washington D.C., and hundreds of enslaved people rented from plantation owners quarried the stone, cut the timber and laid the bricks, dawn to dusk, with no wages, whipped if they slowed down. Most are not even named in the records, just negro hired. When it was finished in 1800 and President Adams moved in, the enslaved workers were sent back to the plantations with no credit and no freedom, and for the next 65 years more enslaved people worked there. Some of you thought the white man built that.

We built cities in Egypt and did not dwell in them, and we built the White House and cannot dwell in it. The same curse, in ancient Egypt and in spiritual Egypt.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:16
precepts.why:
Exodus 1:14 says “they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field”. We were in the fields in ancient Egypt; we were not just building pyramids. They had us doing plantation work and cropping there too. Deuteronomy 28:16 is that curse: “Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.”

The same way ancient Egypt made us slaves and worked us in the fields with all manner of service, in America that curse also fell upon us. We were cursed in the cotton field, in the sugar cane field, in the tobacco field, with five year olds and two year olds picking cotton. Our lives were made bitter, and that is why we eat the bitter herbs at Passover: they represent our lives being bitter in Egypt.

And all manner of service: we were their servants, cooking their food, watching their kids, entertaining them. Sing, this Hebrew got a good voice, sing me one of the songs of Zion. That is what we do here in Babylon. Some of you drive a bus, fix the road, drive a taxi cab: servant jobs, and you don't see it. We have been slaves so long we got comfortable with the jobs they give us. We are kings and priests; we are not supposed to serve any nation. Our job is to serve God.

Read the curses of Deuteronomy 28 and then read what happened to us in ancient Egypt, and you will see they are the same. America is spiritual Egypt.

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:17
precepts.why:
Exodus 1:12 says “the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.” No matter how much they afflicted us, we kept multiplying and growing. And what does it mean that the Egyptians were grieved because of us? They were mad; they were angry.

Leviticus 26:17 explains it: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.” To be grieved because of the children of Israel means they hated us, and they that hated us reigned over us.

The same way the ancient Egyptians hated us, the so-called white man hated us when we were brought here as slaves. So “the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour”: they did not play with us. In ancient Egypt they beat the hell out of us with whips, and in America the same: runaways caught and whooped, lynchings, and still lynching us. Not only America but all the lands we were scattered into are Egypt, but this is the main one, Mystery Babylon.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:18
precepts.why:
Pharaoh told the Hebrew midwives, “if it be a son, then ye shall kill him”. Where is that in Deuteronomy? “Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land”. What is the fruit of our body? Our children. That is why it says our children are going to be cursed.

In ancient Egypt, when the baby came out, Pharaoh commanded the midwives to kill it if it was a male. That is oppression. Today they do the same thing, and it is called abortion.

And how do they get rid of the males today? The school to prison pipeline. They create conditions for our people to live in poverty, bring drugs into the community, and when the brothers are out there selling, they put them away for the rest of their lives. That whole system was set up by Esau. That is them dealing wisely, “let us deal wisely with them.” And through the vaccines: when you look at the rate of autism in young black and Hispanic men, it is very high. They put things in the vaccines to mess with the babies' minds. But Esau has been mixing with us, so some of our DNA is in theirs, and now white people complain that their kids are coming out with autism too.

It goes back to the scripture that says they try to destroy the poor secretly. Secretly they try to kill every male child amongst us, because they are trying to stop the prophets from coming on the earth. What Pharaoh did in ancient Egypt, America is doing in spiritual Egypt.

precepts.label: Isaiah 41:14
precepts.why:
The Bible says God is a man of war. War is coming to this place; God is bringing war to the earth. And we should not be afraid of it. Isaiah 41: “For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee. Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”. God is talking to us. Don't be afraid; he is going to help us.

Read on: “Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff”. A new sharp threshing instrument is a weapon, a weapon of war. The mountains are the nations, and we are going to beat them small. “Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them”. A time is coming when we will say, there was a place named America; what happened to it? It will be wiped out and never remembered again.

So when war comes, we should be celebrating, happy, not sad, because through those wars our salvation and our freedom come. We should pray for that thing. Our job now is to prepare for it, spiritually and mentally, not physically: prepare ourselves and our people, and keep a food pantry, as Bishop has been teaching for a while.

That preparing is spiritual warfare: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh”; the weapons of our warfare are “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Don't get caught up in the foolishness of this place, the marches and the stupidity, even with your own family. Stay in the scripture, cast down every evil imagination in the minds of our people, and bring every thought “to the obedience of Christ”, the black Messiah. The man of war fights for us.

precepts.label: Psalms 2:8-10
precepts.why:
Leviticus 25:46 says of the heathen bondmen, “ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you”. Hold that, and hear Psalm 2: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.”

The Lord is saying, don’t worry, it is going back to that. He is going to give us the heathen for our inheritance. Meaning what? We are going to own them. That is what it is saying right there. We were their possession, but they were originally our possession; we sinned against our God and became theirs, and it is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

“Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” If they don’t want to get right, boom, upside the head. “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.”

So the inheritance of Leviticus 25:46 and the inheritance of Psalm 2:8 are the same: the heathen given to Israel for an inheritance and a possession, ruled with a rod of iron.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:14
precepts.why:
Leviticus 25:46 says “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? Forever. Esau thinks he can change his judgment. No. No. You cannot change it. God said it, it is in writing, it is stamped. So that means you are going back into slavery.

“I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.” Whatever God does is forever. Nothing can be put to it to change it, nor anything taken from it. There it is: that men should fear before him.

Isaiah shows it coming to pass: “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” For servants and handmaids, because that is the role the Lord gave them, and for how long? Forever. The judgment of Leviticus 25:44-46 cannot be undone.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
In the wilderness the children of Israel wept and said, “We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. What are they saying? Deuteronomy 28:48 explains it.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Serving our enemies in hunger and in thirst is one of the curses that was upon us, and it was also a curse that was on us in ancient Egypt. We had to serve the Egyptians for the want of all things. It is the same today: you need money to buy food, and you have to serve for it.

Back then we had fish, because the Nile was abundant in fish, and we had melons. So brothers got delivered from oppression and started talking about going back to Egypt: even though we were oppressed, at least there we had some good food. It is the same thing with us here in America. A lot of you have food, you are full, you are comfortable. Well, for now.

precepts.label: Leviticus 18:3
precepts.why:
It was not just that the Egyptians fed us. Everything we learned, we learned from the Egyptians back then. So when we came out of Egypt, God said: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do”.

Why did God say not to do after the doings of Egypt? Because we learned the Egyptian customs while we were there, the Egyptian names of the week. It is the same way here in America: you talk about Monday and Tuesday and all of that, days named after their gods, and all that is idolatry.

So God says, everything you learned in Egypt, forget it. The people who longed for the fish and the melons of Egypt were still holding on to Egypt in their hearts. And it is going to be the same thing when we are delivered up out of here, out of spiritual Egypt: everything we learned from this land, we will have to leave behind.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:28
precepts.why:
“Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.” If you get blessed, it is to have to give to him that needeth. That is biblical, and that is part of the wisdom of Deuteronomy 4:6: the laws, statutes and commandments, everything written in the scripture, are our wisdom and our understanding, and we are to govern and deal with each other based on what God says.

How is that giving set up? You read it in Acts 2 and Acts 4: you put it at the feet of the leadership, and the leadership distributes as there is need. The leaders in the body initiate everything by the scripture, with the fundraising initiatives and the different offices, so that the body can be self-sustaining.

But many of us were raised in this environment and have not sharpened our senses, so we conduct business like Esau. Israelite businesses pop up, market to the body and make money off the body, and never come back and say, my pockets have gotten filled, my business has become profitable, I want to give back. Some even have cutthroat tactics, with no type of respect, moving the same way the world moves.

Those who say they are businessmen should read how the economics in Israel functioned and how we dealt with each other. Debt was forgiven every seven years so that debt would not pass from generation to generation. There was no usury, meaning no interest. Today what people wind up leaving behind is debt, and their families become responsible for it.

So the righteous way is to labour, prosper, and give back to the needy among our people. That is the foundation for seeing how Babylon, Esau and the rest of the world move in buying and selling, and why a nation that keeps God's statutes would be called “a wise and understanding people.”

precepts.label: Hosea 12:7
precepts.why:
“He is a merchant, the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress.” That spirit was in Israel as well, and this is spoken to us. Hosea deals primarily with the northern kingdom, with Judah mentioned in the mix.

Where did we learn it? Not from our own law. When you read the law and how we handled economics amongst ourselves, there was no such thing. We were mixed among the other nations and took on their customs: not only their lewdness and fornications, but how they would have no compassion on their people and how they dealt with them.

Usury was something we were supposed to do to the other nations: we lent to them and charged them interest. When we dealt with each other it was different. Not that you did not make a profit, but there were ways we dealt with each other, always with the intent that we would have communal wealth, so that generations would not get stuck with bad habits. We looked out for each other, the same way the corners of the field were left to help one another, and we were still able to prosper under that.

Instead we took up the insatiable appetite of the nations, having to get every last drop. Not so with God. That is why these balances of deceit were spoken against us. Keeping the statutes, dealing righteously with our brethren, is the wisdom Deuteronomy 4:6 says the nations will one day see in us.

precepts.label: Amos 8:5
precepts.why:
“When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?” That is messing with the scales. It is the same spirit of deceitful balances read in Hosea 12:7, and it was spoken against us because we had mixed among the other nations and learned it from them.

Remember when Nehemiah had to curse out the merchants from the other nations because they came to sell on the sabbath. If we had all been in the spirit, would he have had to curse them out? We would not have bought, and they would not have come. They came because we were breaking the law by buying.

We should not have that spirit, but now you see who really does. One of the grand ways they falsify the balances today is with the oil: they call Venezuela's crude too heavy, while it is more profitable to them than anything else.

It reaches into the mortgage too. Interest is designed to keep you in debt and keep you broke, and the mortgage is loaded front heavy, so the first years go mostly to interest and not principal. On a 300,000 home a 30-year loan costs an extra 250,800, and instead of fixing the economy Trump talks about a 50-year mortgage, where you pay an additional 476,000 just to have a cheaper payment, and leave that debt to your wife and kids. That is the deceit. When we think of scales we think of the little scale at the fruit market, but this shows how broad that evil principle is. Edom does it first, and they excel at it.

It is not wrong to own a home; it is better than renting. But the system is broken and was never supposed to be that way. If our economics were set up by the law, we would lend to each other without usury and own our homes. Even to that extent the Lord had righteous weights, scales and balances, and that is the wisdom and understanding Deuteronomy 4:6 speaks of.

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:15 says that if we will not hearken unto the voice of the Lord to do all his commandments and his statutes, “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. Verse 27 names one of them: “The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt”. That is what we need to see. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 did not just come out of nowhere. A lot of them are the same curses that were on us in ancient Egypt: the botch of Egypt, the diseases of Egypt, the oppression of Egypt. God said in Exodus 3:9, “I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.” Our forefathers were oppressed in ancient Egypt, and they were oppressed here in America, and are still being oppressed here. The oppression is real.

So when the scripture calls America spiritually Egypt, it is because the same things that happened to us in ancient Egypt happened to us here, and the curses show it. The diseases of Egypt cleave unto us in this land, along with the rest: we grope at noonday, we do not prosper in our ways, and as a nation of people we are only oppressed and spoiled evermore.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:14
precepts.why:
Officer Tatum was asked if black men like him were better off during slavery, and he answered, 100 percent. He said that after slavery there was an explosion of success, black Wall Street, men married to the women they had children with, and now look at the inner cities. What he does not understand is that he thinks white people just switched and started loving us after they let us out of slavery.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”. When Christ returns, these same people who had us in slavery, and have us in slavery, are going to try to fight against Christ.

“their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” These same slave owners rejoice to devour the poor, and they do it secretly. Even though slavery supposedly ended with the emancipation proclamation in 1863, then what? You had the school to prison pipeline. Redlining. Sundown towns. Sharecropping. It is still the same thing.

Look at us now, and why? Because he is setting up all these traps. That is why he is still oppressing us to this day, and that is the “yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” But Tatum cannot see that.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:32
precepts.why:
Habakkuk said their rejoicing is “to devour the poor secretly.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people. We are the poor that they are devouring secretly. The poor are Israel, and it is Zion that the Lord founded for them to trust in.

Tatum blames the murders, the violent crime and the abortions in the inner cities on our people alone. But who legalized abortion? The white people. Who started Planned Parenthood with Margaret Sanger? He just skips past that; according to him they are not the cause. That is the secret devouring of the poor, and it is the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48 still on our neck.

precepts.label: Acts 24:16
precepts.why:
Tatum said black people need to do better: y’all whole life is activism, y’all still complaining and protesting like y’all still slaves. Why were the brothers in Ocean Springs, Mississippi? Because one of our brothers, Nolan Wells, had a mysterious death with a bunch of white people around it, in a town known for lynching black people. Yes, we are activists. Yes, we stand up for righteousness and speak against the evils and atrocities that happen to our people. That puts fear in our oppressors, and he is doing their bidding: hey, you’ve been cooning great lately.

So what is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.”

We always have to do what is right toward God and toward our people. Better looks like getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your family. What is better than that? That is what a conscience void of offence looks like, and he is not speaking from the point of a black man.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 9:27
precepts.why:
“Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them”. That is what happened to us: we have been delivered into the hands of our enemies, the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”. That is what is happening now. The Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance; that is what the Bible tells us to do.

“and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” How is that happening? By the purple and gold going to this city and that city, this country and that country, teaching the word of God. These are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

So when we see these things happen to our people, yes, we are going to be there, and no, we are not going to stop. We don’t care if we have coons among our own people; we are going to rise up and save the day, because that is how God ordained it. Tatum is mad about it. Get mad. You hate your people and you hate your God.

precepts.label: Exodus 7:4
precepts.why:
A 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, went into Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family lived, and every one of them had to leave when the sun went down. A resident said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march, I don’t like.

They do not like it when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, our respect and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid. We have been marching; Marcus Garvey was marching back in the day.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” Mine armies. We have been marching since Egypt, and we marched around the walls of Jericho.

Israel came out of Egypt as the armies of the Lord, by great judgments on the ones who held them. That is why our marching troubles our oppressors.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:11
precepts.why:
They do not like when we stand up on our feet with confidence as the nation of Israel, not as blacks, but as the nation of Israel.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

Great fear falls on them when they see us rise up as the children of God, as the army of the living God. That is what the man in Cicero feared when he said he could not stand the ones who march, and it is what puts fear in our oppressors when the brothers show up in a town like Ocean Springs. The yoke of iron destroyed us, but the Spirit of life from God stands us back on our feet.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 17:9
precepts.why:
Tatum claimed he had not seen black Hebrew Israelites going out and saying anything in the community when a black man died. That is a lie; he has been found a liar. That is what we do literally every week. We teach in the hoods and the ghettos where our people are: O Block in Chicago, East St. Louis, Memphis, Miami, Compton, LA, Philly. We go toe to toe and face our people.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

They taught in Judah: we go to our people just like the forefathers did. They had the book of the law of the Lord with them: we bring the Bible with us. They went throughout all the cities: we do not just go to one city or one state. Wherever our people are scattered, wherever our people are being afflicted, we are there, teaching the people.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:24
precepts.why:
A pastor named Pam declared that the gospel cannot be for one ethnicity only, that it cannot be just for black men or for white men, and that this is a heretical doctrine preached by false, cultic ministries. Either the cultic ministries are right or Jesus is right; somebody is wrong. It’s you, Pam.

“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

It is only for one nation, twelve tribes. If you are not part of that, you are not getting in. Some of our people are bugged the hell out, and it is a direct correlation to slavery. A white pastor even said God blessed black Americans through white people and slavery, and Tatum agrees with that. But Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the same people under the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:12
precepts.why:
The holy city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

Praises to the Most High for that. The kingdom is only for God’s people. The gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, and no other nation’s name is written there.

That settles what Pam called heresy. Christ was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the city he brings has twelve gates for the twelve tribes. The same people the Lord sent into bondage with a yoke of iron upon their neck are the people whose names are on the gates.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:2
precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. The Lord will bring you into captivity again, because Egypt represents bondage. What does Egypt represent? The first commandment tells you.

“I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.”

Egypt is the house of bondage: the house of slavery, the house of captivity. Egypt and slavery are synonymous. So when the curse says into Egypt again, it means into slavery again.

And it says with ships. Not imaginary ships, not planes, not trains, not a blimp or a hot air balloon: with ships. Ships will be used during this Egypt. And the Lord says it is “by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”: that Egypt as a nation, the one we walked into the first time, we will never see again as slaves. That is done. This Egypt is by boats, and “there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”, slave men and slave women, sold from those ships to the same enemies who put a yoke of iron upon our neck in verse 48.

Last of all, “and no man shall buy you”. The first time, the Lord brought us out of the house of bondage by Moses, and before that we had Samson and Gideon save us. This slavery, nobody. No Nat Turner, no Gabriel Prosser, no Toussaint Louverture, no Dessalines, no Nanny of the Maroons, no Medgar Evers, no Martin, no Malcolm. Only the Lord will do it, through his son. Christ said, I will come down there and save you.

precepts.label: Exodus 14:13
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”. Moses is being very specific, and Exodus 14:13 explains it. At the Red Sea he told the people: “Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.”

The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again, for ever. So when Moses says we will go into Egypt a second time, the Egypt he is speaking of cannot be ancient Egypt. The people would have said, Egypt again? We are going back to Egypt a second time? And he explains: I am not talking about the Egypt you just came out of. The way whereof I speak unto thee, thou shalt see it no more again. It is a different Egypt.

And this time we go into it with ships. Moses saw the end. The Lord showed him the Israelites thrown on cargo slave ships and brought here to America: the transatlantic slave trade. Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So going into Egypt again means going into captivity, misery and tribulation again, carried there on ships, sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. That is why Revelation 11:8 calls the great city, Mystery Babylon, America, spiritually Egypt.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:22-24
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 29:22 speaks of “the generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you”. Who is that? Isaiah 66 shows it: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” The seed and the name that remain in the new heaven and new earth are the righteous of our people that make it, those of us that get the kingdom.

“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” After they come up to worship, “they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”. Go forth where? To look on this place, America. That is the same moment Deuteronomy 29 describes, when the generation to come and the stranger from a far land see the plagues of that land, “brimstone, and salt, and burning”, and ask, “Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land?”

After somebody dies, their carcase is supposed to just disappear. So this is letting you know it is something spiritual. “for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” They are in damnation, cast in hell, being tormented. That is why Deuteronomy 29 says the Lord will separate the man that did not repent unto evil.

There is a place of torment, and it will be set up when Christ returns. After this place is destroyed physically, a spiritual prison and damnation will be set up here, the place of torment for the devils that said, have you come to torment us before our time. Christ has the power over hell and death: he can give you life and immortality, or wake you up and torment you.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:2
precepts.why:
Christ has the power over life and death, which is why Daniel 12 says some shall awake. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Many of them are going to awake. Some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die, you go to sleep, yes. But Christ has the power to wake your behind up and torment you.

That is what stands behind the carcases of Isaiah 66:24, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched, and behind the land of Deuteronomy 29 that is all brimstone, salt and burning. Those who forsook the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers and served other gods do not simply die and disappear: they are awakened to shame and everlasting contempt. As 2 Esdras 9 says, read in the same moment, those who despised his law while the place of repentance was open “must know it after death by pain.” And the righteous awake to everlasting life, the seed and the name that remain.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:26-27
precepts.why:
In Deuteronomy 31 Moses says, “For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves”, and “evil will befall you in the latter days”. How is Moses able to say I know? Deuteronomy 4 shows what he saw.

“I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.” When we went into the land of Israel, our days were not going to be prolonged in it; we were going to be destroyed from off that land. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” Moses saw the Israelites being scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

He could see it because God showed it to him. In 2 Esdras 14, read right after, the Lord says, “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt”, and he held him on the mount a long season, the forty days and forty nights, and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Moses saw the secrets of the beginning, which is how he wrote Genesis, and he saw the end.

So Moses saw what would happen to us in the time of the Babylonians, the Greeks and the Romans, and he saw us here in America, in the transatlantic slave trade, and America being destroyed. That is why he could say with certainty that evil would befall us in the latter days: he had already seen it.

thread.label: Judges 2:11-13
thread.text: And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served Baalim:

precepts.label: Hosea 2:8
precepts.why:
Judges says Israel “served Baalim” and “forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt”. Hosea shows how ungrateful that was: “For she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal.”

That is what the Lord did for Israel. He clothed us, gave us land, gave us food and possessions, all of that. And we turned around and prepared it for Baal; we started serving the devil with what God gave us. Baal, Baalim, it is the same thing: the Canaanite god of fertility, storms, thunder and lightning, worshipped in horrible ways, whose name means lord or master. He sounds like Thor. Baal and Ashtaroth have taken on so many names over the ages, which is why we rarely hear of them, but the worship is coming back to light.

Even now it goes on. Just days before this class, thousands of Afro-Brazilians gathered on a Rio beach to offer gifts to a sea goddess, Yemanja, revered in the Yoruba religion as the mother of all orishas and humanity. Brazil is the tribe of Asher. It is the same deity all throughout: “the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven”. Ashtaroth, the queen of heaven, Yemanja, whatever the name. Our people carried that witchcraft with them and kept doing it, even in Africa.

That's our history, and that is why we are in captivity today, catching hell. The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshipping the devil, and we wonder why America goes down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries.

precepts.label: Leviticus 18:21
precepts.why:
“And thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.” Molech worship went along with the fertility gods: it dealt with children, with the womb. That is what we were doing, and it is exactly what God told us not to do. We became bullheaded and stubborn and started worshipping the devil. That is how Israel “forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.”

Stubbornness runs through this whole history. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” So we have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine's Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. It has nothing to do with us. God did not give it to us.

“Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn”. That is why God's laws are taught without going to the left or the right: we know how we got over here, through stubbornness. If we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

It is how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no judge, no leader, in place, they go back to their lonesome: the officer's not here, the captain's not here, the Deacon's not here, the Bishop ain't here. If you can't uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, the same judgment is your future. Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” Stubbornness is idolatry; it is satanic worship. So many think they are not dabbling in the mystic arts, but when you are stubborn and rebellious, you are: “sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone”.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:23
precepts.why:
Judges 2:19 ends: “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal. 1 Samuel 15:23 says what stubbornness really is.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” Bullheaded, stubborn, is idolatry. It is satanic worship.

That is how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers.” Whenever there is not a judge, a leader, in place, they go to their lonesome. They get relaxed: the officer is not here, the captain is not here, the deacon is not here, the bishop ain’t here, let’s go back to our lonesome. If that is your spirit, you are going to get the same judgment. If you can’t uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction.

Ecclesiasticus 30:12, read just before, gives the remedy: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn.” That is why God’s laws are taught without going to the left or to the right, and without playing games. We know how we got over here: through stubbornness. So if we want to get delivered, we have to wake the hell up.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:8
precepts.why:
1 Samuel 15:23 said rebellion is as witchcraft and stubbornness is as idolatry. Revelation 21:8 shows where the witches and the idolaters end up.

“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone.”

A lot of y’all think, I’m not dabbling in the mystic arts. Yes, you are. When you are stubborn and rebellious, yes, you are. It says sorcerers and idolaters. The one who in Judges 2:19 would not cease “from their stubborn way” is standing with the sorcerers and the idolaters, and their part is the lake of fire.

Psalms 78:8 makes the connection plain: “a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright.” “The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle. They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law.” That is the northern kingdom, though Judah did the same thing. Even when they got over here to the Americas they still did not keep the covenant, and that is why Assyria took the northern kingdom and why Columbus and Cortez came: because of the idolatry. The Lord was sick of it and still is, and this is the last time.

precepts.label: Baruch 2:30
precepts.why:
Solomon prays, “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”. Bethink is not a common word we use today. Baruch clears it up easily: “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.”

“For I knew that they would not hear me”: that is why he put us in captivity, because we are a stiffnecked people. He delivered us to the enemy, by ships, “unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. This land is the land of our enemy: our enemy conquered us and made this land his land. Far is here, far from Jerusalem; near is Africa or Madagascar, colonised just the same.

“but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” In our captivity, in the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves. That is what bethink means: remember, call to mind. Solomon saw in the spirit our people put on the ships and scattered all over the world, yokes put upon our necks, and destroyed so much that we would turn our own eyes against our own people and attack them. He saw that we would lose ourselves and our identity, and try to seek others or recreate ourselves, instead of in the image of God.

So first we must remember ourselves. We can only say “We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness” if we know who we are. And once you learn who you are, you learn who the enemy is by default. As long as you don’t know who you are, you will make your own people from the continent or the Caribbean your enemy, while the white man gets a pass.

Kings tells what the northern kingdom did: “they left all the commandments of the Lord their God, and made them molten images, even two calves, and made a grove, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.” They made false gods; they served Satan, the devil. They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire: today we call it abortion, which is murder. They used divination and enchantments, witchcraft, and “sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the Lord”. So the Lord removed them out of his sight.

Our people were always into idolatry, and Hosea says it in one line: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Joined to idols. Idols, idols, idols. Leave him alone.

And it is still so today. You get it in Santería, brujería, Catholicism; this is what our people, the northern kingdom, the so-called Latinos, are into. That is why the curses keep following us: we want to celebrate witchcraft and idolatry, and the Most High is jacking us up, with earthquakes, puppet presidents and our lands being taken. Why? Because we don't learn. It is all to bring us back to repentance and to the remembrance of who we are.

precepts.label: Isaiah 44:28
precepts.why:
Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire, the old Persian kingdom, in 550 BC, and it was an ancient Iranian empire. That makes this very significant for what is going on today. “the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, and Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem”.

The Lord was working through King Cyrus. The Lord did speak to him, and he listened. Isaiah had already named him: “That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.”

So the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah was fulfilled through a Persian, an Iranian king, called by God his shepherd, who performed all his pleasure: Jerusalem built again and the foundation of the temple laid.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:1
precepts.why:
Isaiah goes on: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

That is why Cyrus could say, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”. The Lord held his right hand and subdued nations before him. The Lord used King Cyrus, who was a Persian, to allow us to go back and build the temple.

Cyrus is also the one who gave that decree. And the kingdom he ruled, Persia and Media, is Iran today, which is why his story is very significant for what is going on now.

thread.text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.

precepts.label: Psalms 10:17
precepts.why:
“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What is the heart? The mind. Ezra had prepared his mind to seek the Lord his God. We are in captivity, always working and tired; some days you get stressed. But the Most High has to remind us that we are living in the last days. So brothers, prepare your minds; sisters, prepare your minds.

David shows who the Lord prepares: “Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear”. We are the humble. We are supposed to humble ourselves to whatever the Bible says we ought to do.

And when we humble ourselves, the Lord hears our desire and prepares our hearts. We will prepare our minds. That is what Ezra did before he went to teach Israel, and that is what is required of us now, as we watch Iran and Israel go to war and America get involved, and more of our people wake up and repent.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:17
precepts.why:
Why prepare our minds and our spirits? Because war is imminent. We are seeing Iran and Israel at war and America getting involved, and the wars are only going to get worse. What we see right now is a birthing pain. Yet all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

Sirach says: “They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight”. All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord.

That is Ezra's example: a heart prepared, and a soul humbled in the Lord's sight, ready to seek the law, do it, and teach it, whatever comes.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:3-4
precepts.why:
Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law and to teach it. Sirach shows why: “A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” We must trust in the laws of God, and the law will be faithful unto us.

“Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard”. We have to prepare what to say. Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics.

“and bind up instruction, and then make answer.” Bind up the instruction first, and then make answer. That is how Ezra could teach in Israel statutes and judgments: he had prepared his heart before he opened his mouth.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17
precepts.why:
This is to the brothers who teach, the up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. Ezra prepared his heart to teach in Israel, and the Lord says: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, and it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

Habakkuk shows the watchman's posture: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. He is awake and paying attention. As watchmen we must be faithful and pay attention to the signs of the times, hear the word at the Lord's mouth, and give Israel warning from him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 2:1
precepts.why:
Satan said to the Lord about Job, “Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” Job's life was blessed, and Satan brought it all out before the Lord: “But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” Sirach shows that this is not only Job's story: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.”

As soon as we give our life to the Lord, the Lord forgives us of our sins, we repent, and we start to do the work. We get involved, we study, we clean our lives up according to the commandments. And while the Lord is sitting on the throne, Satan comes up and says, have you considered your servant such and such, or sister such and such? They've been doing real well. Yeah, they are doing good right now, but I guarantee you, if you let me do A, B or C to them, they are going to curse you. They are going to leave the truth, blaspheme your name, and go right back to me and white Jesus.

And the Lord says, all right, go ahead, you can try. Don't kill them; don't take their life. Just as he said to Satan about Job, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.”

Then came Job's trials, one messenger right on top of another. The Sabeans took the oxen and the asses and slew the servants: the first trial, his businesses and finances. The fire burned up the sheep and the servants: the second, his business and finances again. The Chaldeans carried away the camels: the third. Then a great wind smote the house and his sons and daughters were dead: the fourth, his family. That is what it means to prepare your soul for temptation. The pattern Job went through is the same one every servant who comes to the Lord goes through today.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 37:19
precepts.why:
Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's friends, tells him, “Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” You were the one that strengthened men and women when they were weak; your words upheld those that fell down in grief and in sin. “But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.” Now judgment has come upon you, Job, and now you have given up, you have lost the spirit. Where is that mighty man that helped all the people? Now you're upset, your lips stuck out, you got an attitude.

Sirach says it plainly, and it is something we should all be mindful of: “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” That is what Eliphaz was telling Job. You were the guy that comforted everybody, but now that your turn has come, now that judgment has come upon you, you are fainting and want to give up.

And Job had been that man. He remembered the days “When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”: the commandment is a lamp and the law is light. He was a judge who sat in the gate; young men hid themselves and the aged stood up when he came. “I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” He knew what to say to the dying and “caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” “I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame. I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.”

That is how Job represents the twelve tribes. What Job went through, we go through as a nation of people, because we were the servants of God, and when the trials came, we gave up, gave in to sin and turned our back on the Lord. The one who taught many has to be profitable to himself when his own trial comes.

precepts.why:
Job 20:6 says of the wicked, “Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds”. That is space travel and planes, and Isaiah 14 shows the same man. What Job's friend Zophar says here is prophetic.

“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”. That is space travel. I will exalt my throne: see the American flag. They didn't put their flag on the moon for Africans or for Latinos. That's for America.

“I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: that is slavery in North America, the sides of the north where we were taken. “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: that is planes. “I will be like the most High”: I'll be like God.

So when Job 20 says his excellency mounts up to the heavens and his head reaches the clouds, it is this man who said in his heart he would ascend into heaven and be like the Most High. And it goes on: “Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where is he?” When God destroys this man, this hypocrite, all his ascending will not save him.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:18
precepts.why:
Job 20 says of the wicked man, “He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.” Imagine it: this man is going to be like a dream when he is taken off the earth. Another name for a vision of the night is a nightmare. Dealing under this white man, God said, when you wake up it's going to be like a nightmare was chased away, and you are going to look for that man and he's going to be gone. “The eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.”

He is going to be off the earth, and Obadiah says how: “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.”

Who spoke it? The Lord hath spoken it. That ain't what we said; the Lord spoke that thing. Many Israelites are becoming like Israelite Christians: scriptures like this, and like what we are reading in Job, they purposely ignore, and say, no, we're just going to read the love scriptures, find the scriptures where all the nations are there. They try to change the narrative of what God is saying. But God says there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.

And then “His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.” So don't worry about reparations. Everything this white man took from us, his hands shall restore. The Vatican holds a lot of gold, silver, and all our records: we are going to get everything back.

Sirach is the precept: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. Though he humble himself, and go crouching”. That is him bowing down to you. Remember in DC, the police and white folks bowing to Black Lives Matter, hugging, kissing and crying, and a lot of blacks and Latinos said, see, they love us, they're humbling themselves to us. The Pope apologized for slavery and kissed feet, and the Africans said, he loves us. But did the Vatican not steal all the wealth from us and keep our records secret? Are they giving the wealth back? “yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass”. You ever see a dirty glass and you wipe it so you can see? Kramer from Seinfeld, a show our people loved and laughed through, went on a frenzy cursing black people out, that forty years ago you were hanging from a tree. precepts.label: Isaiah 14:16
precepts.why:
Job 20:22 says, “In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.” Watch Isaiah 14: “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”. That is what they are going to say in that day about the man who shook the kingdoms of the earth.

And this is important, because there are black Hebrew Israelites saying we are going to commit this wickedness. But what did it say? Every hand of the wicked. This is proof that we are not going to be doing this. It is the other nations that are going to attack America for the atrocities, for all the bombings, for all the displacement. They attack us as though we are the problem, and they don't realize the Most High is going to raise up the other nations to come against them, and they are going to entreat them very, very bad. Every hand of the wicked shall do this, not us walking in righteousness.

Then “When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him”: when they shall say peace and safety, then sudden destruction.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:13-19
precepts.why:
Isaiah 13 tells what is going to happen to the man they look narrowly upon. “Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth shall remove out of her place”: when Christ returns, the earth is going to move off her axis, “in the wrath of the Lord of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.”

“And it shall be as the chased roe”: the Edomite shall be as a chased roe, and a roe is a deer; “and as a sheep that no man taketh up”, a sheep that nobody tries to save. “they shall every man turn to his own people, and flee every one into his own land. Every one that is found shall be thrust through”: every Edomite that is found. “and every one that is joined unto them shall fall by the sword”: you want to keep your little Edomite friends? You are going to get it too. The nations ain't going to play.

“Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes”: the little hybrid babies, the little mixed kids. No mercy. “their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished.”

“Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them”: that's over in Iran and Kurdistan, “which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.” We don't care about your money, America, your 300 billion; they want revenge. “Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.”

“And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms”: Babylon is the United States of America, the best country on the planet, and it “shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” That is Job 20:22, every hand of the wicked coming upon him, and Job 20:29: “This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.” That is the portion of the white man, of Esau, Edom: his heritage is destruction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 6:23
precepts.why:
Job looks back on his life: “Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me; When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”. When his candle shined upon my head: the Holy Spirit was on me. But what does “by his light I walked through darkness” mean?

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandment is the lamp, and the law is the light.

That is the light Job walked by. We can only walk through darkness the way Job did: with God’s commandments. Job kept the law, and that law was the light that carried him through a dark world.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 29:29
precepts.why:
“As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle”. What is the secret of God? This shows the relationship between Job and us.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

God reveals his secrets to the Israelites. The things revealed belong to us and to our children for ever, and they are revealed for a purpose: that we may do all the words of this law. The secret of God was upon Job’s tabernacle because he was of that people, and he kept that law.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 16:18
precepts.why:
“When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!” What does that mean, he prepared his seat in the street?

“Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.”

So Job was a judge. He sat in the gate and judged the people with just judgment. That is why “The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up. The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.” When Job rolled on the scene, everybody shut the hell up. Princes covered their mouths, young men moved the hell out of the way, and the old men stood up and saluted him. The nobles held their peace; they had nothing to say either. That is total respect and honor.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 10:18
precepts.why:
“Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” Job is telling you what he used to do. The fatherless are the orphans, and he delivered them and the ones who had no one to help.

That goes into God’s law: “He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.”

Job judged the way God judges. And he did not stop there: “The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” When somebody is about to die and wants to speak to you, sometimes you are at a loss for words and do not know what to say to bring them comfort. Job knew exactly what to say. Then he comforted the widow, mourning and crying because her husband just died.

That is a hard thing. You have to pray to the Lord: give me the words. You have to let a dying believer know, it is going to be okay; even when you leave this world, you are going to be all right. When we die, that is not the end of it for us, and that is what comforts us.

precepts.label: John 5:39
precepts.why:
“I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.” Whatever Job did not know, he searched out. Sometimes brothers try to fake stuff. Don’t fake it. Job said, if I did not know it, I searched it out.

Christ said it: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.”

We have to get to that point. Search it out. Get the Who’s Who with the Apocrypha, get your Zondervan Bible dictionary, get the complete works of Josephus, get your concordance, and do your own work. Before you ask us a question, how about you search it out, and then ask your question after you have done research on it. That is what Job did with every cause he did not know.

precepts.label: Acts 17:11
precepts.why:
“These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

That was the attribute Job had: “the cause which I knew not I searched out.” The Bereans received the word with all readiness of mind, and they searched the scriptures daily to see whether the things they were taught were so. That made them more noble.

We have to be the same way. Search things out daily. Do not just hear it and move on, and do not come asking without having looked first. A father to the poor, a judge in the gate, and a man who searched out what he did not know: that is the kind of man Job was, and the kind we have to become.

precepts.label: Exodus 18:19
precepts.why:
“My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand. Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.” Job was up there. He was no pushover, no punk.

This is what Jethro told Moses: “Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God”.

That is what Job was doing. He was for the people to God-ward, bringing their causes to God, and men waited in silence for his counsel. “After my words they spake not again”: after Job spoke, you had nothing to say. “I chose out their way, and sat chief”: he counseled them and directed them, and dwelt as a king in the army.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:2
precepts.why:
“And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.” They waited for his words with their mouths open. When he was teaching or giving counsel, he was dropping blessings on them, dropping understanding.

It says the same thing as the song of Moses: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”.

So when Job spoke, it was like that: “my speech dropped upon them.” And that right there is prophetic. It is going to come again in the future, near to come.

precepts.label: Psalms 132:9
precepts.why:
“I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.” That shows you how Job used to dress. The way he dressed, that is how his righteousness reflected.

“Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

That is why it was written down beside Job 29:14. Sometimes you just scribble in your Bible, and when you look at it again you see why. God wants his priests clothed with righteousness, and Job put on righteousness and it clothed him. His outward robe and diadem matched the righteousness he walked in, and the saints shout for joy when the righteous are clothed that way.

thread.label: Job 35:9
thread.text: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:29
precepts.why:
Elihu tells Job: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.” This was Elihu speaking to Job prophetically about times to come. Are we not oppressed today? Yes.

Moses wrote the same thing in the curses: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore”. That is what Elihu was talking about. The oppressed crying out by reason of the arm of the mighty is Israel under the curses, oppressed and spoiled evermore.

Solomon said it too: “So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power”. They have the guns, the nuclear weapons, the court system; they have it all, and we have nothing. That is the arm of the mighty.

But the Most High “looked down from the height of his sanctuary” to “hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death”. We are the prisoner: sons of God in a weak body, ruled and dominated by a wicked race of people and subject to their laws. We groan waiting for “the redemption of our body”. We want our godhood back, rulership back, dominion back, to reign on this planet like we once did.

precepts.label: Psalms 56:5-6
precepts.why:
The wicked sits in the secret places and “his eyes are privily set against the poor.” David describes how they watch: “Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil. They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul.”

But the Lord “disappointeth the devices of the crafty”, and “he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth”: from the lies of their media.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:21
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them.” That sounds just like Malachi 4: “the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”, and “it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Nuclear fire is coming to America. precepts.label: Isaiah 35:3-4
precepts.why:
David prays, “raise me up, that I may requite them”: raise me up the third day, so I can get vengeance on the traitor who ate of my bread. Isaiah tells the faithful to hold on for that vengeance: “Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.”

In every IUIC school some brothers may be weak and feeble, spiritually. Build them up. You have to build your inner circle up, loyal and faithful brothers who know the scriptures and fear God, and then have a circle outside of that of trustworthy, loyal men, so that when Jacob's trouble comes you don't all fall.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”. Brothers and sisters, be strong, because at times you might get afraid, but the Lord has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

Then: “behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” We must believe that our God will come with vengeance. A recompence is a requital, the same word as “that I may requite them” in the psalm: an appropriate return for wrongdoing.

Isaiah 47 shows that vengeance on Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”. All these fake Christians talking about America being a Christian society: their nakedness is uncovered by the word of God, and all their shameful deeds are revealed. “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” Christ is not coming back meeting them as a man. So strengthen the weak, fear not, and wait on the God who comes with recompence to save us.
