And that's why the Lord said, “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first.” It isn't Judah over in Africa or in Saudi Arabia. It's Judah here. This history you should be proud of.

precepts.label: Psalms 137:7-8
precepts.why:
Zion “dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Who is the daughter of Babylon? David answers: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” E D O M: that's the red people, the ones called so-called white folks. “Rase it” means destroy it, destroy it, even to the foundation.

Then watch what David calls Edom: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”. Edom is the daughter of Babylon, and Edom is destined to be destroyed. “happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.”

So Judah is dwelling with Edom, the daughter of Babylon, here in the land of the north. The same Edom is the one the vision of Obadiah is spoken “concerning”, and the class went on from here to show America in the Bible through Edom: the pride of their heart, exalting themselves as the eagle, setting their nest among the stars. The daughter of Babylon Zion is called to flee from is Edom in America, and her end is to be destroyed and rewarded as she served Israel.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:7
precepts.why:
“And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah”. Judah is going to be the teachers. “and bring him unto his people”: Judah is the one the spirit comes on first, to go and gather the tribes. “let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.”

We just read that, and then we go back to Zechariah: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The Zion there is Judah, and Moses' blessing lines up with it. Judah is called out first, brought unto his people, and God is his help from his enemies, the daughter of Babylon he is dwelling with.

That is why the next words of Zechariah are about those enemies: “he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” He that touches Israel touches the apple of God's eye. The Lord promised to help Judah from his enemies, and in Zechariah he sends his hand against the nations which spoiled us.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:9
precepts.why:
Zechariah 2:9 says “I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants”. Write this down: the servants there is us. Right now we are their servants. God will shake his hand upon the nations, and the nations shall be a spoil to their servants. The wording might be difficult for some of us, so here is a precept to explain it further.

“Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation”. See that: “the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.” Possess them means own those nations.

So when we go back to Zechariah, “they shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me.” The servants are Israel, the remnant of God's people. The nations that made us serve are going to be spoiled by us and possessed by us. America is described as Babylon, the land of the north, and the day is coming when the ones who served there will spoil it.

thread.label: Zechariah 3:8-10
thread.text: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5-6
precepts.why:
In the Persian captivity there was Joshua the high priest, of the tribe of Levi, and Zerubbabel the governor, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord speaks to Joshua and his fellows, “for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Christ, and Jeremiah 23 shows it.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The righteous Branch raised unto David is Christ, the King who will reign and execute justice.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” That is the same day Zechariah speaks of. The stone laid before Joshua with its seven eyes, and those eyes are the angels. “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”: that is Christ dying on the cross. And “In that day”, every man shall call his neighbour “under the vine and under the fig tree”: that is in the kingdom, when Israel dwells safely under the Branch.

precepts.label: Zechariah 6:12-13
precepts.why:
The Branch appears again in Zechariah 6: “Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord.” That is not the second temple; it is about the third and the fourth.

“Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” Both is the priesthood and the kingship. He sits and rules on his throne as a king, and he is a priest on that same throne.

That is why Zechariah 3 speaks to Joshua the high priest, and why Zerubbabel the governor stands alongside him: the priest from Levi and the ruler from Judah. Christ fulfilled both offices, the priesthood and the kingship, in one man, the Branch.

precepts.label: Genesis 49:10
precepts.why:
The priesthood and the kingship that Christ fulfilled go back to Jacob's blessing on Judah: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the kingship shall not depart from Judah. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: that is the priesthood, and what is between a man's feet is his rod. It shows Christ would come from the rod. There is no immaculate anything; that is make-believe, Egyptian and Babylonian fairy tales. “until Shiloh come”: that is the Messiah, Christ. “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

Matthew 1 traces the line through the captivity. “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, and so down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch coming out of Zerubbabel, the governor who stood with Joshua the high priest.

In the sit-down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat argued there was a curse on Jechonias that no one of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. But after Babylon came in, that was it: Zedekiah was taken away and his sons were killed, and no king sat on the throne in Israel. There was no king in the time of Christ. When he came, the people loved him so much that they wanted to “take him by force, to make him a king”, and “he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” By the prophets, there would be no more king until Christ returns: the sceptre waits for Shiloh.

thread.label: Zechariah 4:6-9
thread.text: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

precepts.label: Psalms 118:22
precepts.why:
Zerubbabel is the branch in the line of Christ: Matthew's genealogy runs from Zerubbabel through Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan and Jacob to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” So when the Lord speaks to Zerubbabel, he is speaking to the father of Christ's line.

“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Zerubbabel was of the king's bodyguard, one of the top fighters. The Lord is telling him, no, this has nothing to do with your fighting skills; we know you can break bones, but that's not what is going to overcome everything. The spirit of the Lord is what's going to do it.

“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon the great, and it shall become a plain: flattened, destroyed. “and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it”: crying mercy, mercy unto it.

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is that? Christ. He is the headstone. Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel's lineage; Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone.

“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it.” His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. But this goes deeper than that: because of verse 7, verses 6 through 9 are going into the last days as well, when the great mountain, Babylon the great, is brought down to a plain and the headstone, Christ, is brought forth.

thread.label: Zechariah 4:6-7
thread.text: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:24-26
precepts.why:
Zechariah asks, “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain”. Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity, and Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So who is this great mountain? Jeremiah shows where the mountain is: “And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord.”

Watch what he calls Babylon: “Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.” The great mountain is Babylon.

“And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord.” That lets you know it is not Iraq. Are people still living in Iraq today? Yes. This says “thou shalt be desolate for ever”, so it is not talking about ancient Babylon.

So the great mountain before Zerubbabel is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Before him it becomes a plain, flattened and destroyed, and it is done “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Everything we do must be according to the spirit of the Most High God; it has nothing to do with our physical powers and our skills.

precepts.label: Isaiah 19:18-20
precepts.why:
Zechariah says Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who is the headstone? Christ. Why are they crying grace, grace? Isaiah shows it, and shows that Zerubbabel is in these last days as well: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.”

The language of Canaan is the scriptures, and one city shall be destroyed. “In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.” An altar is for sacrifice, and this is talking about where the Israelites are: here in Babylon the great.

“And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.” Who is that saviour? Christ.

So Zechariah is saying the same thing. The headstone is that saviour we just read about in Isaiah, and the crying of grace, grace is because of the oppressor. The great mountain, Babylon the great, becomes a plain before him, and he delivers his people out of the land where they cried.

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 5:8
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:7 ends: “but he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.” He that remaineth is you and I. And on the map, Ekron sits right there above Jerusalem.

What does it mean to be as a Jebusite? “And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David.”

When you read the history, David smote the Jebusites and made them servants. That is what he did. So when Zechariah says “Ekron as a Jebusite”, the land that the Philistines hold will be brought under Israel the way David brought the Jebusites under him.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 9:20-21
precepts.why:
“And all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel, Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.”

They were our servants, our slaves. The Jebusites left in the land did not rule over Israel; Solomon put them under a tribute of bondservice.

So when we go back to the last part of Zechariah 9:7, “and Ekron as a Jebusite”, it means they are going to be our servants. Those that are left of the Philistines will be to Israel what the Jebusites were to David and Solomon, while he that remaineth of Israel “shall be as a governor in Judah.” The pride of the Philistines is cut off, and the order is turned back the way God set it.

precepts.label: Exodus 2:25
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:8: “And I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more: for now have I seen with mine eyes.” No oppressor shall oppress us any more; they will not pass through.

And “now have I seen with mine eyes” is the same as Exodus 2:25: “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.” In Egypt God looked upon Israel under their oppressors and had respect unto them, and then he brought them out.

So when he says now have I seen with mine eyes, he is looking upon us to have respect unto us. The Lord encamps about his house, the oppressor is stopped, and right after it Zechariah says “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion”, because the King comes.

thread.label: Zechariah 9:9-11
thread.text: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.label: Mark 11:4-7
precepts.why:
“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee”. We have to believe our king is coming. He “is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.”

Mark shows the history of what Zechariah was prophesying: “And they went their way, and found the colt tied by the door without in a place where two ways met; and they loose him. And certain of them that stood there said unto them, What do ye, loosing the colt? And they said unto them even as Jesus had commanded: and they let them go. And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.”

So when people say Christ isn't mentioned in the Old Testament, shut up; you don't know what you're talking about. Zechariah saw the King of Zion riding upon the colt, and Mark records Christ sitting upon that colt. He is our King, just and having salvation, and he is coming to the daughter of Zion.

precepts.label: Psalms 72:8
precepts.why:
Zechariah says the King “shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.” David says the same: “He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.” And he reads on: “They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.”

They are scared of the saying from the river to the sea. Well, that's in the Bible too. And it is not just that little area. It is from sea to sea, meaning the whole planet earth is ours. When we went into the land, the Lord gave us that portion according to the number of the children of Israel, but the whole earth really belongs to us, to the ends of the earth.

In that day “I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”, meaning we would have no military during that time. The King's dominion is our defence, and his enemies shall lick the dust.

precepts.label: Hebrews 13:20
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” What is the blood of thy covenant? Hebrews shows it: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant”.

The blood of the everlasting covenant is Christ dying on the cross. By that blood God sends forth his prisoners out of the pit.

If you didn't know it, this is the pit. Like it says, yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death; Ezekiel 37 calls America the valley of dry bones. This is the pit, and “no water” means there is no truth here.

Then Zechariah says, “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”. We are the prisoners of hope, and the stronghold is the Lord, this Bible: “The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.” By Christ's blood we are brought out of the pit to the stronghold.

thread.label: Zechariah 9:12
thread.text: Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee;

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.label: Nahum 1:7
precepts.why:
Zechariah says “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope.” Nahum tells us what that stronghold is: “The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.” The stronghold is the Lord, and that means this Bible.

The verse before in Zechariah speaks of the pit “wherein is no water”, meaning there is no truth. That pit is America, the valley of dry bones of Ezekiel 37. Out of that pit, the prisoners are told to turn to the stronghold.

So turning to the stronghold is turning to the Lord and his word. He is good, he is our strong hold in the day of trouble, and he knows them that trust in him. We are the prisoners of hope, and the Bible calls us that.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:23
precepts.why:
Zechariah says turn you to the stronghold; Proverbs says “Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” God's reproof is his laws.

So there is a stipulation to get God's Holy Spirit: you must turn at God's reproof. The laws come before the spirit. Only when you turn to his laws will he pour out his spirit on you and make known his words to you.

That is why all these dumb Christians that say they have the Holy Spirit and won't keep a commandment do not have it. They have Satan on them. Turning to the stronghold, for us prisoners of hope, means turning at his reproof and keeping his laws.

precepts.label: John 14:15-18
precepts.why:
More proof that the spirit comes after the laws: Christ said the same thing. “If ye love me, keep my commandments. And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”.

Who is that Comforter? “Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.” Then Christ says, “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” He is letting us know he is the Comforter. It ain't Muhammad. Christ is the Comforter; he is the Holy Spirit.

So the one who turns to the stronghold and keeps the commandments is the one who receives Christ, the Spirit of truth. Those who claim the Holy Spirit and keep no commandment do not have him.

People don't reject the truth because it is false; they reject it because it is uncomfortable. Black and Latino people hate the discomfort of change. But knowledge you won't act on just sits there and becomes nothing, like people who say they want to lose weight, know what to do, and won't do a damn thing.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:19-20
precepts.why:
Why does Zechariah call us prisoners of hope? Peter says Christ “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. When Christ came, he preached to the spirits in prison. That's us: our mothers and fathers, our sons and daughters. We are in a spiritual prison.

When Rome was dominating us, that was a prison. We didn't have free rule; Rome was over us.

Those spirits in prison are the ones “Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.” That disobedient people is you and me. We are the prisoners, and our hope is in the stronghold.

precepts.label: Isaiah 61:1
precepts.why:
Isaiah shows what Christ was sent to do for those prisoners: “The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound”.

We are in a prison house, and we are bound in sin. Christ is anointed to proclaim liberty to us captives and to open the prison to us that are bound.

That is why we are prisoners of hope: the prison is real, but the one anointed to open it has come, and we are told to turn to him, the stronghold.

precepts.label: John 8:32-34
precepts.why:
Christ said, “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” They answered him, “We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” So they knew being made free referred to being in bondage. They said, we were never slaves.

They couldn't see that Rome was over them. They were paying taxes to Rome and were oblivious to it, because they were rich and wealthy.

So watch what Christ says: “Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.” He took it down a level: you won't understand what I just said, but you are a servant. You are bound in your sins.

That is the prison of the prisoners of hope: bound under the nations and bound in sin. The truth, turning to the stronghold, is what makes us free.

precepts.label: Romans 6:12-13
precepts.why:
If sin is the prison, Paul tells us how to walk out of it: “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” Don't let sin reign, meaning rule, within you.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.”

Our bodies must be vessels of righteousness, used for the commandments of God and nothing else. That is how the prisoners of hope turn to the stronghold: no longer servants of sin, but instruments of righteousness unto God.

precepts.label: Isaiah 61:7-9
precepts.why:
Zechariah says “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”. Isaiah shows what that double is: “For your shame ye shall have double”. The shame we have suffered in captivity after captivity, we shall have double for it.

“and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion”, because we are a confused people; take a look at TikTok and Instagram. “therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.” God says “I the Lord love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.”

Watch the double we are going to get: “And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” We have never experienced that. Imagine walking down the street and everybody knows your kids' names and moves the hell out of their way: that's brother so-and-so's kid. All people are going to know our children. That's double.

Write down the chain of events: awakening, which is us waking up; followed by tribulation, and we are between those now; World War III; Armageddon in the midst of that war, where Christ makes his advent; deliverance; wilderness; then kings and priests, rulership.

thread.text: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, sait

precepts.label: Malachi 4:4-6
precepts.why:
“Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me”. You may think at first that is only John the Baptist. That is a good thought, but it is the John the Baptist work in the last days, and the end of Malachi shows it.

“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” Then here it comes: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”. That is still the John the Baptist work, but in the last days it is Elijah, sent before that great and dreadful day.

What would he do? “And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children”. Why? Because we would forget who we are. We would lose our way. “And the heart of the children to their fathers”: he is going to show us our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and turn us back to them, “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

So the messenger of Malachi 3 is the messenger sent before the Lord comes to his temple in the last days, to bring a people who forgot themselves back to their fathers and their law before the day of his coming.

precepts.label: Zechariah 13:8-9
precepts.why:
“For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ soap”. Christ is like a refiner's fire. Zechariah shows what that fire and that soap mean.

“And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”. Two out of every three of our people shall be cut off and die. Why? Because we know damn good and well.

“But the third shall be left therein.” There is going to be a third: one third will be saved out of this land, America. “And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. That is the refiner sitting over the silver in Malachi 3, purging the sons of Levi “as gold and silver”.

“They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.” That is the wilderness right there. That is how you know Malachi 3 is the last days: “who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?” Only the third part that comes through the fire refined.

precepts.label: Malachi 1:11
precepts.why:
Malachi 3 ends with the refined people offering again: “Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in former years.” What is the offering of Judah and Jerusalem? Malachi already said it in the first chapter.

“For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the Lord of hosts.”

Incense offered unto his name, and a pure offering. That is the offering in righteousness that the purified sons of Levi will offer after the Lord sits as a refiner and purifier of silver: a pure offering, with his name great from the rising of the sun to the going down of it.

thread.label: Malachi 3:5-6
thread.text: And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against false swearers, and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, a

precepts.label: Exodus 22:18
precepts.why:
“And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers”. That is what we wanted to get to. The law already said what God thinks of sorcery: “Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.”

Look at what our people are doing. Growing numbers of black women in Maryland and across the nation are leaving church worship for what they call ancient forms of spiritual contact. Some call it witchcraft, a term they accept and embrace, offering prayers to spirits and deities like Oshun. More than two hundred witches gathered at a convention in Baltimore. They grew up Christian, Baptist, Episcopal, a grandfather a preacher, a father a deacon, and now they call themselves witches. God said he is going to be a swift witness against the sorcerers.

A sister who used crystals testified that instead of healing you, it entices you and traps you into depending on it for every little thing; it is like a placebo effect. So brothers, be careful. Sisters come in with these crystals and say, oh no, it’s just spirituality. It is witchcraft. Don’t fall for it, or you are going to have demons all up in your house.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 22:22
precepts.why:
“and against the adulterers”. What is adultery? When the brothers had the sit down, the Christian pastors could not explain adultery. The law explains it: “If a man be found lying with a woman married to an husband, then they shall both of them die, both the man that lay with the woman, and the woman: so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.”

A site advertises connecting with swingers of color, black swingers in the lifestyle. This is adultery.

And it happened among us. In San Antonio a sister bought another sister lingerie to spice up her marriage, and invited her and her husband over. They switched partners, and it went on for months without anyone knowing. It only came out when one wife decided she wanted the other husband. The husband left without a wife got mad, and then he revealed it, as if the Holy Spirit came on him. You didn’t reveal it because a spirit told you to; you revealed it because you were mad.

We had to put him out; everybody had to go. Now that brother is on YouTube and TikTok like an all knowing teacher, teaching everything we teach, but he is not going to reveal that he was that swinger brother. God said he will be a swift witness against the adulterers, and so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:12
precepts.why:
“and against false swearers”. What is a false swearer? “And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.”

That goes into perjury and false statements. To swear by his name falsely is to profane the name of our God.

So when God comes near to judgment, he will be a swift witness against the ones who lie under oath and make false statements, the same as against the sorcerers and the adulterers. He is the Lord; he signs the command with his own name, and he will not let his name be profaned.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:13
precepts.why:
“and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages”. You might say to yourself, this does not apply to us; nobody among us oppresses the hireling in his wages. Oh, you would be shocked. It took place right here.

The brothers said, let’s all be truckers. Some got their own authority: I control all this, I’ll hire you, and you, and you. But I like these brothers better, so I’m giving you the good, high paying jobs, and the rest of you I’m not giving too much work.

“Thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning.”

Some brothers were being paid late, and were not getting paid the same amount. Everything was unjust. That is defrauding your neighbour and robbing him, and it is exactly what Malachi says God will be a swift witness against. Don’t get mad; get glad, and get it right.

precepts.label: Exodus 22:22-24
precepts.why:
“and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless”. The law on the widow and the fatherless is heavy: “Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child. If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry”.

“And my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.” Damn. Whoever afflicts the widow and the fatherless, God makes his own wife a widow and his own children fatherless.

Then Malachi finishes: “For I am the Lord, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.” The same God who wrote these laws has not changed, and he still judges the sorcerers, the adulterers, the false swearers and the oppressors. And because he changes not, the sons of Jacob are not consumed. That is why we are still in existence today, the twelve tribes.

thread.text: And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;

precepts.label: John 6:15
precepts.why:
Matthew traces the line “after they were brought to Babylon”: Jechonias begat Salathiel, Salathiel begat Zorobabel, and on down to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch, right through Zerubbabel.

In the sit down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat said there was a curse on Jeconiah that nobody of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. Think. After Jeconiah, was there a king in Israel sitting on the throne? No. When Babylon came in, that was it. Zedekiah came, and they got rid of him and killed him with his sons. There was no king during the time of Christ.

John shows it: “When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” That is how much Israel loved him. They said, we want him to be our king. He said no.

Why? Because the prophets said there would be no more king until Christ returns. The sceptre was held for Shiloh, the Messiah, “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” Christ would not be made king by force before the time, so the line through Jeconiah and Zerubbabel is not ruled out; it runs straight to the one king still to sit on the throne.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 28:5
precepts.why:
How is the kingdom of heaven suffering violence? Is somebody jumping up in the sky punching God in the face? No. David answers it: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” Israel is called the kingdom of the Lord. The throne Solomon sat on was over a nation of people on the earth.

So when Christ says “from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence”, the kingdom of heaven is the nation of Israel. It is our people who suffered the violence.

“and the violent take it by force”. That is Rome. The violent man Christ speaks of is the same one just read in Psalms 140: “preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” They sharpen their tongues like a serpent, and “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their media, their philosophies, their religions, their politics. They have “purposed to overthrow my goings”, and the one whose goings they overthrow is the Israelites.

It is the same man being violent to us today. So what would Jesus say? He already spoke on it: Christ called Rome the violent man. They are the violent, and the kingdom they take by force is Israel.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:1-5
precepts.why:
Christ said the sun would be darkened and the stars would fall from heaven before the sign of the Son of man appears. Ezra shows the same end, and it goes into the land of Israel and those who call themselves Jews and are not being destroyed.

“The days shall come, that they which dwell upon earth shall be taken in a great number”. That is the third woe: billions of people are going to die. “And the way of truth shall be hidden”: who the Israelites are, who the people of that land are, is hidden. “And the land shall be barren of faith. But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” You see how wicked this world is getting; that was prophesied.

“And the land, that thou seest now to have root, shalt thou see wasted suddenly.” The land that has root now is the land of Israel, and it will be destroyed suddenly by the Persians and the Arabs. That goes back to the destruction at noonday. Wasted is the word Isaiah uses: “I have created the waster to destroy.” Seeing the land wasted means nuclear bombs.

“But if the most High grant thee to live, thou shalt see after the third trumpet”: in Revelation the third trump is nuclear war. “That the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night”: a nuclear bomb going off at night looks like the sun shining. That is what the prophet saw. “And the moon thrice in the day”: three bombs going off in the day, at Ekron, Ashdod and Ashkelon. “And blood shall drop out of wood”.

That is why Iran was attacked: they are trying to stop prophecy, or slow it down. But God's counsel shall stand. Iran will develop nuclear warheads, the Arabs will unite, and they will be brought down in the valley of Jehoshaphat. The day of the Lord will not come on us as a thief, because we are watching the signs.

thread.text: Now the first day of the feast of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?

thread.label: Matthew 26:26-29
thread.text: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.

classes.title: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.label: John 1:29
precepts.why:
At the Passover dinner Christ took the cup and said, “For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” The blood the Israelites put on the doorposts in ancient Egypt represented Christ's blood. It represented the new covenant: Christ coming and dying for our sins.

John shows who the lamb is: “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God”. Christ is called the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year represents Christ. He is that sacrifice.

So we do not sacrifice anymore, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today; some brothers are crazy. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God. Believing in Christ and doing what is right is what protects you from the wrath of God.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
The bread represents Christ's body, and the cup his blood “shed for many for the remission of sins.” Paul says it plainly: “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

Christ is our passover. The lamb that was killed represents Christ, and that is saying a lot. He was sacrificed for us; he came and died for our sins.

So you do not have to go kill a lamb and put the blood over the doorpost so that you do not die. You believe in Christ and you keep the commandments, and we come together, we break bread and we drink wine, as Christ did with the twelve at the Passover. That is being under the new covenant.

Don't run, don't cry and lose your dignity; make preparation, and go over there and teach the word, because all things work together for good to them that love God.

thread.label: John 2:19-20
thread.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.

precepts.label: Mark 14:58
precepts.why:
Christ said, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”, and the Jews answered, “Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?” They thought he meant the building.

At his trial the false witnesses brought it back: “We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.” They had overheard his teachings, and they lied on him. He never said he would destroy the temple made with hands.

Even their lie points to the truth: another temple “made without hands.” The temple Christ spoke of raising up in three days was not stone at all. It was his own body, and that is what the rest of the scriptures read here make plain.

precepts.label: Mark 15:29-30
precepts.why:
This is Christ on the cross. “And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, Save thyself, and come down from the cross.”

They mocked him with the very words of John 2:19, still thinking he had boasted about the building in Jerusalem. But there he was, hanging on the cross: the temple he spoke of was being destroyed right in front of them, and they could not see it.

So we know Christ was talking about his body. “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”: they destroyed his body on the cross, and in three days he raised it up again. What the passersby railed at as a failed boast was the prophecy being fulfilled before their eyes.

precepts.label: Matthew 27:63
precepts.why:
After the crucifixion the chief priests and Pharisees came to Pilate, “Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.”

They called him a deceiver, but they remembered exactly what he said, and they understood it: after three days I will rise again. That was what he meant when he said in three days I will rebuild this temple.

They had heard him teach it. So when they put up false witnesses saying he would destroy the temple and build it back, they were lying on him, twisting his words about the building, while among themselves they knew he spoke of rising from the dead. The temple raised up in three days is his body raised the third day.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:21
precepts.why:
This is what he actually said: “From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.” He was talking about raising up himself the third day. Christ's body was the temple.

And his temple today is us. Peter says, “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.” That's the real temple: wherever our people are gathered is a spiritual house. Lively means the laws percolate within us, with zeal, passion and fire, not a boring spirit. Paul says, “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: stones have to come together, so play your position and don't try to change it through deceit. And “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” “for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are”.

How does that temple grow? “Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings, As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. Everybody forgets verse one: you have to put away malice, deceit, jealousies and murmuring first. The sincere milk of the word is the law, and we have to drink it like a baby drinks milk, not once a month or once a week, but constantly. That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves and our communications: we are the temple.

Christ prayed, “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.” Sanctify the Israelites through thy truth, mainly the elect, the apostles he was speaking of. And the truth is the word: “thy word is truth.”

So to know the truth is to know what the word says, and the word that is truth says a day is coming that shall burn as an oven. Knowing that truth is what frees our people from the lies, and it is the first step before the Lord saves the poor of his people from the sword of the nations.

precepts.label: Malachi 4:1

“and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: burnt up like stubble in that day, unless ye repent. “and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch”. Your children will be cut off too.

Psalm 21 sounds just like it: “Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them. Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.” Neither root nor branch left. And Isaiah 14: “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers”. The forefathers committed the crime, took the wealth and everything from us, and now the children are left holding the bag: Esau, and not just Esau, Elam, Ishmael and the Hamites, all got wealthy off the backs of the Israelites and had us in slavery one way or the other. The Lord will “cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew”, the same son and nephew, root and branch.

“For they intended evil against thee: they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” The nations counsel against us, but the Lord takes the crafty in their own craftiness and saves the poor, Israel, from the sword.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:9
precepts.why:
The rulers “commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus”, and again: “Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name?” We read that and say it could never happen in America. Don't fool yourself. It will happen here.

Christ warned it: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” Imagine they shut your bank account down. Now you can't pay your rent, your mortgage, your car note; you lose your car, your home, and maybe your wife: that's what you get for teaching that Bible, don't block Jesus. Everybody says, I'm strong, I can go through it. Wait till that day, with a newborn baby and you can't get infant formula. Some will say, I'm going back to being a Christian so I can get access to my money.

That hatred starts with the followers of Christ, but it applies to all twelve tribes of Israel. Look at the news: black and brown people killed, and they cry, what did we do to these white people? Why did they kill Sandra Bland? Why did they kill Tamir Rice? Christ said you would be hated of all nations. Christ is our king whether you accept it or not, and the white man looks at you and says, these are the people of Christ. You are the children of God, and they are the children of the devil. You might not like it, but it's true.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:14
precepts.why:
Being hated of all nations is not only for those who teach the Bible; Ezra shows who it will affect. “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was paradise in the time of Adam. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

You have to enter those hard things to enter paradise. The angel is telling Ezra that if we don't go through the hardships of Jacob's trouble, we can never get paradise. If you decide to kill yourself before it happens, you cannot get paradise. If you say, I'm going to join another religion to escape punishment from these other nations, you will never receive it.

Read on: “Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. The righteous shall suffer hard things, that is Jacob's trouble, and hope for paradise. “for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The wicked Israelites are going through Jacob's trouble too, but they are not going to see the kingdom.

So when Christ said you shall be hated of all nations, it covers all Israel. Whether you teach or not, the strait things are coming; the only question is whether you come out of them into what is laid up for you. That is why you cannot run from the persecution when they command us not to teach in his name.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:9
precepts.why:
“And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad”. We saw persecution against our brothers in France; it hasn't gotten here yet, and they say America is the major hub. When it happens, can you stand the rain? That's why we say don't take the convocations lightly.

People read these things and say, oh, that's old time. But Solomon says: “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” That's you and me. We read Maccabees and Acts 8:1 and say that could never happen again? You're simple as hell. What happened in 1 Maccabees 1 and Daniel 3 is what Revelation 13 speaks of, no buying and selling, and it leads to death.

Paul said the same thing: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Those old-time things were written for us to learn from, because they are going to happen again. We need patience and the comfort of the scriptures because we are going to go through what our ancestors went through: how did they deal with it, how did they survive?

Herod killed James and, because it pleased them, took Peter also. And Trump joked about bringing back public executions. The Christians don't understand what is about to come; in here we understand, because what has been is what shall be.

thread.label: Acts 7:37-38
thread.text: This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:6-7
precepts.why:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” When Acts 7:38 speaks of “the church in the wilderness”, it is speaking of the government of Christ. That church was Israel, the twelve tribes, and it is his government that rests upon his shoulder.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” Christ is called the everlasting Father because many times in the Old Testament, when you read about the Father, it is making reference to Christ. That is why, when Philip asked Christ to show them the Father, Christ answered that he had been so long time with him and still Philip had not known him. Christ is letting you know: I am the father that created you. Not the Father, but your father.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Increase means it starts small. Christ said the kingdom of heaven starts like a mustard seed, but in the end it is the largest. Once that mustard seed is planted and growing, there is no stopping it. It sits “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

This truth cannot be stopped. No matter how many Israelites they attempt to kill or arrest, the church that was in the wilderness, the government on Christ’s shoulder, keeps increasing and has no end.

precepts.label: Daniel 2:44
precepts.why:
“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.” These kings are the last kings of the image, the ten toes, the ten common markets, and America is that iron and that clay. In their days God sets up his kingdom, and that is what is happening now: Israelites are waking up all over the world.

“Which shall never be destroyed.” That says the same thing as Isaiah 9: “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” The church in the wilderness, the twelve tribes under Christ’s government, is a kingdom God himself sets up, and it will not be brought down.

That is the difference between this truth and the movements of men. Asked in an interview how Israel in Christ differs from the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, SNCC or the Young Lords, the answer was plain: those were all man-made, they all had an end, and most of them do not even exist today. This kingdom is not man-made.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.” The God of heaven set it up, so no government of this world can stop it.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:15-18
precepts.why:
Christ asks, “But whom say ye that I am?” and Peter answers, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Christ tells him “flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.”

Then verse 18 is the key: “upon this rock I will build my church”. That rock is Christ himself, not Peter. And the church he builds is the same government we read of in Isaiah 9, the same church in the wilderness in Acts 7:38: Israel.

“And the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” There is no stopping us. Once you get the proper understanding of the word of God, you cannot stop it; it is going to flourish and grow. The gates of hell will attempt to stop it, but they will not prevail. They attempted it when they murdered Nat Turner, Denmark Vesey and Gabriel Prosser, men who knew they were Israelites. They said kill them, and it did not stop. Through whispers and hushes, this word kept going.

The gates of hell are not a flesh and blood enemy: “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” In our carnal mind we think that if we organize we can overthrow the system, but we cannot. The governments of this earth are set up by Satan, and God allows it. Only God can bring all that down, and Christ has promised that none of it will prevail against his church.

thread.label: Acts 7:43
thread.text: Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.

precepts.label: Amos 5:26
precepts.why:
The Iranians burned large statues of a horned, bull-headed figure bearing the so-called Star of David, and they knew what they were doing: they were burning statues of Baal. That is not the Star of David. You cannot find it anywhere in the Bible; it is a sign in the occult.

Stephen said, “Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.” If you didn't know, Moloch is Baal: the same thing, both the devil. The star is the star of their god, the devil, Baal or Moloch.

Stephen was quoting Amos: “But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Which ye made to yourselves: it is idolatry. God did not give us that star. When King Solomon was dabbling in witchcraft, that is how he got that star; God never gave it to us.

So the star so-called Israel and America carry is the star of Baal, and Baal worship shows up in plain sight: the bull's head statue at the 1933 Chicago World's Fair on Jewish Day, the giant mechanical bull at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, the bull on Wall Street. Even bullheaded, stupidly stubborn, comes from Baal worship, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. That idolatry is why Israel was carried away, and why we are in captivity today.

precepts.label: Micah 4:10
precepts.why:
Paul and Barnabas went about “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The tribulation hasn't fully started; you see it on a certain scale, but it will intensify. It will get worse, and worse, and worse.

Micah says how to go through it: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail”. The Bible says to be in pain. Pain is coming, and it has already begun; pay attention to what Trump and these people are doing. But whatever pain you go through, you still have to labour, labouring in this truth.

“for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”. Where are we living today? Babylon: Mystery Babylon the Great, the United States of America.

Why does it say like a woman in travail? Because the pain comes and it goes, and when the baby is close to coming the pains increase and get worse and worse. That is what you see taking place now. Whether this society has another ten or twenty years, as the time draws nearer the pains will increase: the affliction rising against those of us that fear God. Keep labouring through them.

That is why the brother who is not studying and applying the scriptures has no root and will not survive it; when things get real he will be offended, scared, and go back into the world. Sisters, a brother who never teaches and is never in a camp video is a gamble.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
Much tribulation is coming, and Revelation shows where it comes from: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman”. The dragon is the beast, the white man, Esau. According to the prophecy they will be angry at us, “and went to make war with the remnant of her seed”.

Why? Not because we are evil or terrorists, but because we “keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The testimony of Jesus Christ is everything written in this book, everything the prophets said would happen, everything written about who the wicked are and all the evil the so-called white man is doing. That testimony says these people are the synagogue of Satan, and that God is bringing judgment on them for all their evil on the earth. As you teach it, they get angry and make war with us.

So do not think we will be out there teaching the Bible and everything will be good. The tribulation will be attacks from the government: labelling us a hate group, lying on us, putting us in prison, hitting your pocket and your food, attacking your wife and your children, because those are the things we care about. In the end they will force idol worship: worship the beast, or you can't buy, sell, work, get a job or go to the doctor.

The dragon is wroth, and he will make war with us. That is the much tribulation through which we must enter into the kingdom of God, and why we must be exhorted to continue in the faith.

precepts.why:

That is for all of you online who like to stay home and say, I don't like camps. Do what God said to do. Come in, learn, sit down and be quiet.

Some say, I want to come to the school, but I'm not right yet; I'll come when I get right. When is that going to be? You come to the school to get right; none of us are 100% right, we're all trying to get right. You aren't going to get right in your wicked mama's house or with your homeboys. So “strangers from the covenants of promise” can only be read one way: the covenant of promise is only with Israel.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 46:27
precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:13: “But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who was afar off? We deal with precepts. These Christians like to say, let's go to the Greek, let's go to this book, let's go to that. We stick to the scriptures and stay within our book.

“But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off.” It is Israel who is afar off.

It's really that simple. The ones who were far off and are made nigh by the blood of Christ are Israel. Then verse 14: “For he is our peace.” Our peace, not everybody's peace. Reading from verse 12 down to verse 14, the our becomes plain: these Ephesians in Ephesus are Israelites scattered in Ephesus.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:6-8
precepts.why:
Ephesians says “he is our peace”, so go to the prophecy of the Prince of Peace. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, possessive again. “and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” When it's time for Christ to return and the Israelites to reign, there is not going to be any end to it. “The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

Then: “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.” So our peace is Israel's peace. Christ is the peace that brings both nations, the southern and the northern kingdom, back together. That is the both he made one.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:21-22
precepts.why:
“For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us.” Remember the animal sacrifice that was against us. When Christ came on the scene, he abolished animal sacrifice. And it was never prophesied that Israel would be joined back together through animal sacrifice, but only through Jesus the Christ.

“Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land.” He gathers the children of Israel from among the heathen, so you would have Israelites living in places like Galatia, Ephesus and Colosse.

“And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” That is what Ephesians 2:14 means by made both one.

So he is our peace: the Israelites' peace. These Christians in America do not know what they are talking about. Turning Ephesians 2 into blacks and whites coming together is a racist lie. Christianity is nothing but white supremacy, because it is not backed up with the Bible whatsoever.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:17-20
precepts.why:
“Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children; And walk in love”. “But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints”. Why did Paul write to the Ephesians that way? Because that is what they used to be caught up in. Ephesus was a tough pagan environment. The worship of Diana, Artemis, involved all manner of lewd behaviour: they filled the great theatre, they had orgies, they got drunk, witchcraft, idolatry. Diana is the queen of heaven, the same as Ashtaroth, and the same as the Yoruba goddess, and our people were caught up in it in ancient times and today.

Chapter 4 shows it: “This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind, Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart”.

“Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness. But ye have not so learned Christ”. Paul wrote in that form because he knew the lifestyle they came from, living as the Gentiles.

They were once “Gentiles in the flesh” and “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”, but now made nigh by the blood of Christ, “fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”: the northern kingdom, the so-called Argentinians, Colombians, Brazilians, Venezuelans, Puerto Ricans and Mexicans, the Israelites according to the Bible. So our people need to wake up and repent from the idolatry, the fornication and the lasciviousness, and flee from idolatry, or receive the same judgment coming on America.

thread.text: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.

precepts.label: Nahum 3:1-4
precepts.why:
Christ said the gates of hell shall not prevail against his church. They tried when they murdered Nat Turner and the other men who knew they were Israelites, and through whispers and hushes the word kept going. “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” Sometimes our carnal mind says, if we organize we can overthrow the system. No. The governments of this earth are set up by Satan and God allows it; the Most High “setteth up over it the basest of men.” Only God can bring that pyramid down. We get out by “the foolishness of preaching”.

She spilled the blood of the tribes of Gad, Reuben and Issachar to steal this country, and on the blood of our brothers and sisters she set up churches, courthouses and school institutions to indoctrinate us. This country is full of lies and robbery.

“The noise of a whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of the pransing horses, and of the jumping chariots.” It moves up in time: the whip on the horse, the rattling wheels of the stagecoaches, and the jumping chariots, which are the helicopters. “and there is a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcases; and there is none end of their corpses”: they were slaughtering us.

“Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts”. America is the well-favoured harlot: everybody wants to live in America, and some kissed the ground when they got here and never saw any golden streets. She is the mistress of witchcrafts, and that is the gates of hell. “that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts”: the nations she sold were the two kingdoms of Judah and Ephraim. That is the spiritual wickedness in high places, and it shall not prevail.
