precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 9:9
precepts.why:
The first vial brings “a noisome and grievous sore.” Noisome means foul smelling, harmful, noxious, extremely offensive to the senses, particularly the smell: a real nasty sore. It is the same plague that came on ancient Egypt, a boil breaking forth upon man and upon beast throughout all the land.

The record shows what noisome looks like on a man. When the Lord struck the wicked king Antiochus, “the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” His flesh fell off him and his stink offended his whole army.

What could make a man get like that? A nuclear bomb explosion causes severe radiation burns, known as cutaneous radiation injury, that frequently lead to intense itching, blistering and open sores. The burns come in stages: first redness and swelling, then a latent phase, then severe blistering and deep, long lasting necrotic ulcers. When a nuclear bomb goes off and the blast does not kill you, you are going to be rotten, your skin falling off, and it is going to be noisome.

That is how we know this first plague belongs to that one hour, when the destruction comes on America, modern day Egypt: the same kind of sore that ate Antiochus alive falls on the men who have the mark of the beast.

precepts.label: Psalms 91:1-3
precepts.why:
The key thing in the verse is who the sore falls on: “upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image.” If it is only them, where are we? What happened to us? We are delivered.

Psalms 91 explains why. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” If you dwell in the secret place of the Most High, you dwell in his shadow, meaning his protection. “I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

“Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.” That is the first plague, the noisome pestilence, and the Lord will deliver you from it. That is why the scripture says the plague fell only on those that worship the beast and have his mark: because we are delivered.

This plague is coming in that one hour, and in that one hour, when the bombs are falling, it is not going to come near us. The radioactive waves, the noisome pestilence, the poisoned water will not touch us, because the Lord is going to deliver us up out of here. The same pestilence that destroys America passes over the people who dwell under his shadow.

precepts.why:
“And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon the great river Euphrates; and the water thereof was dried up”. The Euphrates runs from Iraq up through Syria to Turkey, and it is drying up right now, from severe droughts, with dams along it; whoever controls the water controls the agriculture. So don't tell us the Bible isn't true. We are in these days, the time is now. You won't read this in the Quran, the Gilgamesh epic or the Egyptian Book of the Dead; you only read it in the Bible.

So “that the way of the kings of the east might be prepared.” Ezra shows who the kings of the east are: “Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” The dragons of Arabia are the Arabs.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Carmanians are Iran, the Iranians. And the land of the Assyrians here is Israel: they are going to waste a portion of the land of Israel.

Then come the three unclean spirits out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet: politics with NATO, the financial system of the United States, and Christianity. “For they are the spirits of devils, working miracles, which go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.” Those three spirits, all coming from the white man, are leading to war on top of war like we have never seen, and the way is being prepared for the kings of the east.

The nations, NATO among them, will besiege America and pour out all their wrath upon her. “Then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her.”

Revelation tells the same thing: “And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning, Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.”

The smoke that goes up unto heaven in Ezra is the smoke of her burning in Revelation. The ones about her that bewail her are the kings of the earth who lived deliciously with her, standing afar off in fear. Her judgment comes in one hour.

Then “they that remain under her shall do service unto them that have put her in fear”: prisoners of war. And the party is not over. After the fall of Babylon, the Lord bends Judah for him, fills the bow with Ephraim, and raises up the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece.

precepts.label: Isaiah 19:20
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. Who is this great multitude that is over us? It is law enforcement, their military, set over the believing Israelites. Isaiah proves it.

“In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof”. This Egypt is a spiritual Egypt: America. An altar is used for sacrifice, so there is going to be a lot of death. “And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors”.

Why would we cry unto the Lord? Because of the oppressors, with an s on it: more than one. That is the great multitude whose burning wrath is kindled over us. That is Jacob's trouble, and we have not gotten to that part yet.

So the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16 is the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the power of spiritual Egypt that will be over our people in this land, and it is because of them that Israel will cry unto the Lord.

precepts.label: Joel 2:17
precepts.why:
Joel shows the same cry. “Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly”, and “Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

Why will we cry, Spare thy people? We just read it in Isaiah 19: because of the oppressors. They will say, we killed you, where is your God? We cut your throat, we ended your bank account, where is your God?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He pities his people because we are not in the land. But he promises not to leave us alone: “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil”, “and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen”.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”. That is the name the Bible gives to the power that is going to be on us: the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16, is the northern army. He will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, the Dead Sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, the Mediterranean, “and his stink shall come up”. The white man shall meet death when he goes to that land, because he has done evil things.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” Spell that word: i-d-l-e. “Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.”

Idle means a person avoiding work: lazy, indolent, slothful, shiftless, inactive, sluggish, lethargic; without purpose or effect. Those words fit some of you in here, men and women. Not the new people who just came, but those who have been with us two years or more. What are you doing? Do you have an office? Is there something you are doing here in Israel? If not, you are idle, and idleness teaches much evil.

And what will the idle be fed? Things offered unto idols, i-d-o-l: an image or representation of a god used as an object of worship. Look at the images of the Roman Catholic Church; those are idols. One word: Christianity.

So the ones the multitude takes away and feeds with idolatry are the ones with no purpose in here. Because you were idle, you will be seduced and given Christianity, that idolatrous religion. Stay busy in the work of the Most High.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 35:5
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the Lord gave the ungodly “place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them”. Their malice is their hatred for us, shown in all the sins they have committed against us, and it is still going on: innocent blood shed again in Springfield, Illinois, a woman who called the police for help and ended up murdered in her own house. How do you call the police for help and they kill you?

Ezekiel names that malice: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. While we are here struggling and suffering, they are still killing us.

That is why the Lord executes judgment on them “by little and little”: a flood here, a fire there, an earthquake here, a war there. He is not ignorant of what they are; he created them, so he knows their pedigree. “Their cogitation would never be changed”: their way of thinking, the hatred they have for us, cannot change. That is why the cop shot the man and said he did not even know why he shot him. It is in them.

It was there from the beginning: “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” He made up his mind from young to kill Jacob, and that thought has continued from generation to generation. It started with Cain and Abel, for Esau is Cain regenerated. That is the perpetual hatred.

“For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon”. There is no pardon and no grace for Esau. His neck is on the chopping block, and the judgment coming to America will not change however much they jump, yell and shout. This land is Esau’s kingdom and we are just living in it, so do not set your affection on it.

Idolatry is going into your stubbornness, your bullheadedness, and your disdain for God’s commandments. Setting your own will above the commandments is the beginning, the cause and the end of all evil.

So Paul gives the answer to it: “Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.” Do what? Flee from idolatry. Do not stand there and bargain with it; run from it.

This comes as the Lord promises to gather his people: “I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country”, and bring them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, “and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.” The twelve tribes scattered over here until the time of restoration have to flee their idols, their stubbornness and their disdain for the law, to be that people.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:3
precepts.why:
Sirach says “I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.” With a war between America and Iran unfolding and many prophecies being fulfilled, we look at what the Bible says about prophecy itself.

“Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand.” Blessed is he that reads and hears, and keeps the things written therein. What is written in the scriptures? The laws of the Most High God.

So the blessing is not only in reading the prophecy but in keeping the law. We are blessed when we read and keep the things written in the law, because the time is at hand, and the doctrine poured out as prophecy was left for all ages, including ours.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:19-21
precepts.why:
“I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.” Peter says, “We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed”. Take heed to do what the scriptures say. The Most High called us into this truth, so we have to take heed.

“as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place. That is why Christ said, let your light so shine before men. We have to be that example for our people, to win them over into the faith. Whether you are in DC, New Orleans, California or the UK, the Most High chose us, and through our example we have to win our people over.

“Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” Prophecy is the foretelling of future events in the Bible, and it did not come by the will of man. Holy men of God, holy black men, holy Hispanic men, spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. That is the light sent forth afar off.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:1-5
precepts.why:
“Behold, speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put in thy mouth, saith the Lord”. Speak in the ears of my people. That is why in Ezekiel he said not to go to a people of a strange speech: we have to deal with our people.

“And cause them to be written in paper: for they are faithful and true.” Everything written in the Bible is faithful and true.

“Fear not the imaginations against thee, let not the incredulity of them trouble thee, that speak against thee. For all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness.” Do not fear what the nations are going to do to us for teaching against America and against governments. The Bible says do not fear.

“Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” The Most High says he is going to bring judgment upon the world. That is the doctrine Sirach says was poured out as prophecy and left to all ages, and we do not labour for ourselves only: we speak it in the ears of our people.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 15:7-8
precepts.why:
When we teach the Bible and bring out the prophecy, in the street or in classes, what are these scriptures supposed to do for our people? The prophet told King Asa: “Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.” The days we are living in now are not the time for us to be weak.

“And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim”. When Asa heard the words of the prophecy, he took courage.

That is what prophecy is supposed to do for us: give us the courage to let go of our idols and our secret sins. We are seeing prophecy unravel right before our eyes: Iran and Israel going to war, and now America getting involved. It was a rumor and talk for years, and now we see it unfold. That means more Israelites are repenting, and more of our brothers and our people are waking up. That is the doctrine poured out as prophecy, laboured for all them that seek wisdom.

precepts.label: Sirach 38:17-19
precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” Every class is preparing you for what is coming: rent, mortgage, food and gas are going sky-high, ten dollars a gallon, and you will not get a raise. Can you change it? Then why worry about it? “Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Stress and worry have killed many, and you are no different.

Sirach shows what heaviness does: “Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” This is speaking of when somebody passes: mourn, and then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Heaviness, stress, brings death. And the heaviness of the heart breaks strength: stress makes a man weak. When you are stressed, you don’t want to work out, you don’t want to go to work. Some people eat more; you gain weight, you become fat and sloppy, you lay back, and eventually it is death.

So, brothers, do not let stress wear you down so that you don’t want to do the Most High’s work. Some of you have sat here five or six years in regular clothes. You see the prophecies coming to pass, wars all over the place, World War III a matter of time, and you still sit there. What are you waiting for? What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself.

When correction comes, push harder; prove to Messiah you are still in the fight. Don’t hold grudges and keep to yourself, because that is when Satan messes with your head. A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance, but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken. The Most High is doing his part. It is time we do ours.

precepts.label: Sirach 39:26
precepts.why:
The curse says we would serve our enemies in hunger, thirst, nakedness and want of all things. Why does it target those things specifically? Sirach names the chief things in life: “The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.”

When you target those things, you dehumanize people. You take away the principal things needful for life, for them to be dignified, and those things are robbed from them. That is why they will never let the resources in their so-called backyard be in the control of the people that own them. They must maintain that dominance, the same here and the same in Africa. We see it with Venezuela and Cuba. Our understanding of this scripture is often United States-based, but when you go to these other countries to give the sense, the people are fully aware of the robbing of their resources, and it must be brought to light.

“All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.” Because we have not repented, those things are turned over to the ungodly, and we will not reclaim them until the redeemer comes. In the meantime we must repent and keep the laws, statutes and commandments.

That is why “The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.” You think violence has to be a sword, a bomb or a bullet. Defraud people of those principal things and you are a man of blood. Economic violence is still violence. “He that taketh away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.” Like the brother in the documentary who works all day and still has no money to eat: their only profit is labour.

Lamentations says the same: “We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us.” You see it now in Cuba, in Venezuela, in parts of Africa. Chains don’t have to be chains anymore.

Rome was such “that, whom they would help to a kingdom, those reign; and whom again they would, they displace”: this is where America got the idea of the coup, of destabilizing countries. Judas Maccabeus was catching so much hell from the Greeks that he went to Rome for help, and these are the articles Rome gave him.

“If there come first any war upon the Romans or any of their confederates throughout all their dominion, The people of the Jews shall help them, as the time shall be appointed, with all their heart: Neither shall they give any thing unto them that make war upon them, or aid them with victuals, weapons, money, or ships, as it hath seemed good unto the Romans”. No food, no weapons, no money, no ships to the other side. Today that is called a sanction. That is why they cut Cuba off and forbid all countries to help Cuba; that is why America told the Caribbean, get rid of the Cuban doctors or we cut off your food supply, and the Caribbean said, we need you, but you have to go.

“In the same manner also, if war come first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall help them with all their heart”: America will help you with all their heart, as long as you are theirs. “According to these articles did the Romans make a covenant with the people of the Jews.” It is the same today: America makes articles with countries, and this is where they got it from.

So when you hear about rebel forces, ask where the money and weapons come from: America, Britain, France or Israel, always one of these European powers. The new president of Syria was an al-Qaeda rebel commander with a $10 million bounty on his head, cleaned up and given a haircut. precepts.why:
The prayer is that God would “give you all an heart to serve him, and to do his will, with a good courage and a willing mind.” If you want to return, if you want to repent, he will give you a heart to serve him and to keep his law and commandments. And it must be with a willing mind. Paul shows what that means.

“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of”: though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, because all the glory goes back to the Father. “For necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up, so they can repent, come out of it, and cast away their iniquities. Woe unto us if we preach not the gospel.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” We have to do this thing willingly. Nobody can force you. If you do it willingly you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. “But if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” If you do it against your will, he will take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside those doors in the midst of wickedness and evil again.

So we have to serve the Lord with a willing mind, a sincere heart, and loyalty. We have to come out of all the wickedness we learned here in America, from under the hypnosis given to us here, and serve him willingly.

precepts.label: Isaiah 59:1-2
precepts.why:
The prayer asks God to “send you peace, And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.” You wonder why you have no peace in your life right now, why you are all over the place? Because you are not serving him, not keeping his law and commandments in sincerity. Isaiah shows what keeps us from being one with God.

“Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save.” His hand is not so short that he can’t reach down and help you when you are afflicted or in trouble. “Neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear.” His ear is not so heavy that he can’t hear your prayers and your cries and come down and get you out of that situation.

“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” That is what separates you from your God: your sins, your iniquities. That is the only way he separates himself from you, if you are in the midst of sin.

But if you are doing what you are supposed to do, keeping the law of commandments in the faith of Christ, he is going to come to you, send you peace, and hear your prayers. If you are sincere and honest with him, walking right in his sight, waking up and returning to him, he will never forsake you in time of trouble. He will help you through your hard times.
